findings.subject: C01 launch message
findings.text: C01's launch message held a third call, a foreground log append before the launch pair, against FR2-03 (a)'s two calls. The append ended before C01's call began; C01 ran once (exit 0, retries 0, wall 2.0 s), its timer was the pair's second call, and every later launch held two calls. No effect on the bound, the order or any record; the outcome should keep it as a recorded launch deviation.

findings.subject: MC37's start has no PID receipt
findings.text: C15's other start is one subprocess.Popen audit event of the bound interpreter (-I -S -B -c ...). No record keeps its PID, so FC-P3 could not probe it (failure_capture.no_pair). The start and its cleanup rest on the passing test's own evidence: killpg answered EPERM while the child was unreaped and ESRCH after Popen.wait reaped it. The count is exact only for the audited route (FC-P7); the outcome should say so rather than cite a receipt.

findings.subject: simulated receipts with positive PIDs
findings.text: The MC10 harness (C03 to C05) wrote supervisor-shaped receipts with PIDs 999990001 and 999990002. They are above Darwin's PID_MAX (99999), the records are labelled mocked, no audit event exists and every zero_process_starts check holds, so they are simulated, not starts. A literal reading of P07 section 4 over every S7 record would count them; the outcome and its portable copies should name them as simulated.

findings.subject: timer lines not on disk
findings.text: The bound timer writes nothing by design, so no file holds its 72 lines; the Director's log states 'every timer: exit-file' as a summary. The audit decided the bound from the records instead (FR2-03 (b)): the 72 commands ran strictly in the frozen order without overlap, and the largest wall time, 7.98 s (C17), is far below every outer bound (120 to 600 s). If S9 cites the timer lines, it should keep them from the session transcript.

findings.subject: unaudited routes
findings.text: 'No other program started' holds for the routes the audit hooks see. The provider's 100 bound Git reads (C06 15, C07 25, C17 60) have audit events but no receipts or probes, and their own children are not observed; the non-Python commands (P00 shasum, P05 and Q03 git status, C08 and C10 git archive, C09 and C11 tar, D01 sh with mkdir and cp) run without any hook. This is the frozen design (recorded, not bounded; FC-P7). For C08 to C11 the audit confirmed independently that each extracted tree equals its commit's tree.

findings.subject: the quartet's mocked label lives outside the cohort records
findings.text: outcomes.json records the four coordinator seams as pass with no label; 'mocked' comes from the freeze's controls table (MC26) and from the test source (format_check.run_process patched, class docstring 'Mocked child seams'). P07 section 6 requires the four results to stay labelled mocks, so the MH outcome must carry the label explicitly.

findings.subject: loader deprecation warning on stderr
findings.text: Every Node start that uses the module loader writes Node's 417-byte ExperimentalWarning that --experimental-loader may be removed (stderr of C17's three cases, MC30-probe and MC36, and inside H01's and H02's refusal text). It is not an error and no frozen predicate depends on it; the contract's argv keeps --experimental-loader, which a later Node release may drop. A note for MR and R04, not for MH.

findings.subject: one HOST descriptor is relative
findings.text: HOST's runtime.node_source.content.extracted is the only descriptor whose path is relative ('bin/node', relative to the runtime directory, copied from NODE-SOURCE.json); a generic recomputation of every descriptor reads it as absent. Its digest equals the bound Node. Documentation only.
